source.title: Estimating Neural Representation Alignment from Sparsely Sampled Inputs and Features
source.authors: Chanwoo Chun; Abdulkadir Canatar; SueYeon Chung; Daniel D. Lee

record.tranche_reason: The study's own analyses show that estimated representation alignment can be strongly affected by feature sampling and by the CKA estimator, refining how alignment measurements should be interpreted.
record.gate_note: The study does not test whether alignment rises with model scale or capability, cross-modal vision-language convergence, seed convergence, interchangeable representations, or recurring features. Its relevant results concern CKA estimation under input and feature sampling. Numerical values read only from plots are marked figure only.
record.test_reason: The study argues, with theory, synthetic data and brain-to-CNN comparisons, that measured CKA alignment depends on the estimator and on feature sample size and dimensionality. This bears on V6's measure dependence. It has no model-to-model scaling, seed, cross-modal, mapping or feature-universality tests.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors add that underestimation is worst for high-dimensional or semantically complex representations, such as V4 and IT.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops and evaluates a feature-sampling-corrected CKA estimator; it does not reproduce either original source's convergence experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment estimates vary with feature sample size and estimator choice; the reported bias also depends on representation intrinsic dimensionality. The study additionally varies stimulus sample size, but does not state a textual outcome for each estimator in that sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: Within-animal and cross-animal brain alignment: conventional estimators underestimate a true CKA of 1. With CKAC, cross-animal similarity falls from V1 (about 0.6) through V4 (about 0.45) to IT (about 0.3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Brain-to-brain representational similarity decreases along the ventral stream, and feature undersampling biases conventional CKA downward.

fits_no_version.finding: Between-category CKA decreases from V1 to IT (disentanglement). Trial-to-trial similarity is lower in IT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Object-category representations disentangle progressively along the primate ventral stream.

record.problems: Most empirical results are presented as plots without tabulated numeric values or uncertainty estimates. The neural comparisons use two monkeys; the paper does not test other broad similarity metrics, model scale or capability, or out-of-distribution inputs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result rows omitted.

untested.parts: There is no model scale or capability sweep and no model-to-model comparison across architectures.
There is no vision-language paired-data comparison.
There is no comparison across seeds.
There is no mapping, stitching or relative-representation test.
There is no test of recurring features or circuits.
The study covers only CKA variants. It does not test mutual-kNN or other metrics, neighbour counts, out-of-distribution inputs, or model-to-model convergence.
It does not test plateauing or shared-data explanations.

missing.what: With CKAC, CNN-to-brain alignment for all three regions sits similarly close to the animal-to-animal ceiling. The authors say other estimators cannot reliably show this, so estimator choice changes the substantive conclusion.
missing.locator: Figure 4 left panels; Brain-to-Model alignment section

missing.what: Theoretical result (Eq. 8): CKAS bias scales as 1/sqrt((1+(γa-1)/Qa)(1+(γb-1)/Qb)), independent of the true alignment.
missing.locator: Bias of the Existing Estimator, Eq. 8

record.verdict_notes: This is a methods paper on CKA bias from feature subsampling. Its relevance to V6 is indirect: no model-to-model convergence is measured, only synthetic and brain-to-CNN comparisons. Many record rows are brain-to-brain or own-method results and have been unlinked. The record's states were coded relative to recovering the true CKA; they are re-coded here relative to V6's setting dependence. The bias runs toward underestimating alignment, the opposite of an inflation concern.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, nor comparison of independently trained models across architectures, objectives, or data.
No paired image-caption comparison or scaling of vision and language models.
No comparison of networks trained from different initializations.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test.
No test for recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
The study varies feature and stimulus sample sizes and compares CKA estimators, but does not test other broad similarity metrics, neighbour-count settings, or out-of-distribution inputs.
It does not test whether model-to-model convergence plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain it.

relation.reason: The study directly evaluates estimator and feature-sampling dependence relevant to V6.

tranche.reason: Theory and experiments show that conventional CKA comparisons require qualification for feature sampling and representation dimensionality.

source_check.notes: CKAC retains bias from nonlinear operations; the authors describe it as substantially less biased, not exactly unbiased. The empirical comparisons here concern synthetic populations and brain-to-model alignment, not model-to-model convergence with scale.

statements.correction: CKAC corrects the feature-sampling bias in the synthetic examples; all estimators are similar for CNN-to-V1 comparisons; conventional estimators remain strongly sampling-dependent for V4 and IT.
statements.problem: The study-specific facts are correct, but calling the corrected estimator's performance a challenge to V6 overstates the evidence. It qualifies the scope of sampling dependence.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Finite neuron sampling in the synthetic example and neural-data comparisons
reader_labels.reason: Estimated CKA depends on feature sampling and estimator choice: conventional estimators underestimate alignment, sometimes severely, while CKAC is more stable or recovers the reference value (r5-r8, r9-r27). The study does not compare other broad similarity metrics or out-of-distribution inputs.
